failureModes.invariant: Each base and target path is relative to testdata/api-client-compatibility and resolves to a regular file below that root.
failureModes.rollbackOrEscalation: Reject the fixture update; do not permit the compatibility gate to read arbitrary API definitions.

failureModes.invariant: Two generations of the same language and API fixture must have the same SHA-256 digest.
failureModes.rollbackOrEscalation: Block the generator change and retain the last deterministic renderer.

failureModes.invariant: The computed target client surface must match the expected per-language compatibility classification.
failureModes.rollbackOrEscalation: Classify the removal as source-breaking and preserve an explicit migration path.

failureModes.invariant: Every breaking API pair requires a non-empty acknowledgement id and reason.
failureModes.rollbackOrEscalation: Fail the gate until the API owner records a versioning decision or reverts the breaking fixture.

failureModes.invariant: Base and target outputs for compatible pairs pass every available selected language toolchain; required mode turns unavailable into failure.
failureModes.rollbackOrEscalation: Revert the client renderer regression while retaining the fixture and report evidence.

intentionalLimits.reason: Current JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, and Dart renderers expose options-constrained fields as scalar values, so enum changes remain API compatibility decisions even when the generated source surface is unchanged.

intentionalLimits.surface: success status-code and server JWT requirement
intentionalLimits.reason: Current clients accept the 2xx family and do not synthesize authentication credentials; source compatibility does not imply runtime API compatibility.

rollback: Remove api-client-compatibility-check from aggregate API contract gates and revert its fixtures and report contract together; retain api-client-generation-check and api-client-toolchain-check.
